newsitem.title: USA: Calif tax measure would dampen bond sales - official.
newsitem.headline: Calif tax measure would dampen bond sales - official.

text.p: A tax measure on the November ballot if approved could cool the sales of bonds by local governments in the state, a Los Angeles County official said Friday.
Proposition 218, which is on the November 5 ballot, which would if approved by voters limit the ability of local governments to raise taxes, fees and assesments.
Los Angeles County Supervisor Zev Yaroslavsky told a Bond Buyer California municipal finance conference here that passage of the measure would hurt bonds sales.
When "we look at this (proposition)...we're panic stricken," he said.
The propositon would "put a very severe crimp on local goverments' ability...to meet (their) obligations and to meet the expectations of the public."
Every city and county would be affected by its passage, he said.
"The thing municipalities are going to be able to think about after this passes is how to close the gap--an operating expense gap which clearly we wouldn't issue debt for," he said.

"Whatever discretionary funds that municipalities will have left that could have been used to service long-term debt for capital projects will have to be diverted towards meeting operational cost gaps that will be created by the repeal of some of the assessment districts that have been on the books," he said.
Opponents of the measure have an opportunity to sway voters against it, he added. "This is a wide open election. We have an opportuntiy to beat this thing."
He said Los Angeles County stands to lose tens of millions of dollars if Proposition 218 passes, forcing the already fiscally county to cut servcies even more and "dip into other general funds."
California state Treasurer Matt Fong on Thursday told conference attendees that he has not taken a position on a controversial state tax measure.

During the conference on Thursday other speakers warned of the dire consequences of Proposition 218, which if approved by voters would limit the ability of local governments to raise taxes, fees and assesments.
Several rating agencies and securities firms warned that the approval of the measure could devastate local governments in the state and their credit ratings.
